hypothesis: With the current best synthetic-dev configuration (h_px=1.5, scratch_min_contrast=0.07, scratch_min_length_px=140, boundary_sensitivity=1.0, all else default) on the real Ti64 dev images: (1) worst_consistency_ratio will be <= 1.0. (2) The binding term will be median_rotation_aspect_ratio_rel_diff, not direction or S, because 30-degree resampling blurs thin beta boundaries and changes how laths fragment. (3) median_rotation_direction_diff_deg will be <= 3 deg on images with S >= 0.3. (4) median_rotation_order_abs_diff will be <= 0.03. (5) median_estimator_gap will be <= 0.10. If worst_consistency_ratio > 1 because of the aspect-ratio term while the direction and S terms stay small, the length/width segmentation is grid-dependent on real images even though orientation is not.
rationale:
Why this run now:
- All five iterations were on synthetic data. The real-data half of the question (rotation self-consistency on Ti-6Al-4V, plus the reviewer reading real overlays) has never been tested, and every review flagged this.
- Experiments now run on the Ti64 dev split with worst_consistency_ratio as the target, so this is the first real-image test.
- The iteration-5 configuration is the current candidate: every synthetic dev family is <= 1.0, worst_family is 0.71 and pooled is 0.29.
- Running it unchanged tells us whether the tuning transfers. Changing parameters now would confound that.

Known risks to watch:
- The lowered scratch_min_contrast (0.07) may produce false scratches on real images. On synthetic data it already gave a false scratch on a clean image. On Ti64, colony boundaries and grain-boundary alpha could be taken as scratches. I will check n_scratches per image and the white lines in the drawings.
- The reviewer should check whether colony boundaries are kept and whether grain-boundary alpha is labelled as flakes, which was seen on synthetic images.
- Polarity 'auto' and roi 'auto' are untested on real optical micrographs with resin.

What this run can and cannot show:
- The synthetic results suggest real errors may be in aspect ratio: matched flakes come out about 5-9% too elongated, and harsh images show brick-like cuts. Resampling-induced changes in fragmentation are the most likely way to break consistency.
- Passing the consistency check is necessary, not sufficient. It cannot detect a segmentation that is wrong in the same way at every angle. The overlay review is the only correctness check here.
- Confidence: about 50% that it passes overall; about 75% that the direction and S terms are within tolerance; about 60% that aspect ratio is the binding term.

Still open:
- The synthetic reproducibility problem from iteration 5 (dev list, seed or evaluator changed) is not resolved. The evaluator should log a hash, the seed and the image list, which is an evaluator change, not a method parameter.
- Parallel scratches (recall about 0.08) need a new global Hough/RANSAC line step. No current parameter can fix it.
- A rotation check at several angles (for example 30, 60 and 90 degrees) instead of only 30 would separate grid bias at axis-aligned angles from general resampling loss. That would be a useful extension of the evaluator.
